paragraphs.text: # dsh-pve
简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin for inspecting and managing Proxmox VE (PVE) through conversation, authent
icated with a PVE API token or a username/password (ticket) login.
## Why dsh-pve
- Inspect nodes, QEMU VMs, LXC containers, storage, network, firewall, cluster, backup, HA, replicat

ion, Ceph, users, groups, roles and pools through conversation.
- Manage power state, clone, migrate
, snapshot, resize and move disks, create/delete guests and storages, and manage backup/replication/

firewall rules.
- Every write operation triggers a mandatory native user-approval prompt — the model

cannot bypass it.
- Credentials (API token secret or login password) are kept in the local DSH cred
ential store and never echoed back to the browser or the model.
## Requirements
| Component | Supported baseline |

| Node.js | 20.11 or newer |
| DeepSeek Harness | 0.2.0-rc.1 – 0.2.1-rc.2 (and later 0.2.1 prereleas

es) |
| Proxmox VE | PVE2 JSON API (API Token auth on 6.0+, username/password ticket auth on 5.x) |
## Installation (for the agent)
Once installed, the agent gains 233 `pve_*` tools automatically. Every tool except `pve_sources` tak
es an optional `source` argument.

## Configuration
In DSH Web: **Settings → Plugins → Proxmox VE** (a standalone section on DSH 0.2.0+ hosts).
The page lists your Proxmox VE **sources**. Add one per cluster you want the assistant to reach (for
example production and staging). Each source has:
- **Source name**: required and unique; any language. This is what you (or the assistant) use to pic

k the source.
- **UID**: generated automatically, globally unique, read-only. Credentials are keyed

by it, so renaming a source never loses its keys.
- **Base URL**, e.g. `https://pve.example.com:8006

`.
- **Authentication**: `API Token` (PVE 6.0+) or `Username / password` (PVE 5.x compatible), chose

n independently per source.
- Token mode: **Token ID** (`user@realm!tokenid`, e.g. `monitor@pve!dsh`

) + **Token Secret** (write-only).
- Password mode: **Username** (e.g. `root@pam`) + **Password** (w

rite-only).
- **Skip TLS verification**: enable for self-signed internal hosts (5.x and 6.0+).
Mark one source as the **default**; tool calls that omit `source` use it. With a single source it is
the default automatically.
PVE 6.0+ → create an API token (**Datacenter → Permissions → API Token**) with the least privilege r
equired. PVE 5.x has no API token → switch that source to username/password mode.
### Multiple sources
Every tool accepts an optional `source` argument (a source name or UID). Ask the assistant for "the
staging cluster" and it calls `pve_sources` first to discover the names, then passes `source`. If se
veral sources exist and none is the default, omitting `source` is an error rather than a guess.
For write tools the approval prompt names the target source, and the approval is bound to it: if the
default changes between approval and execution, the write is refused instead of landing on a differ
ent Proxmox VE cluster.
### Upgrading from 0.1.x
Your existing single-source setup keeps working. On first start the plugin turns it into a source na
med `default`, **reusing the same stored Token Secret / login password** (the credentials themselves
are not moved or re-entered). If that automatic step could not run, the settings page shows a "Lega
cy single-source configuration found" notice with an **Import as a source** button.
## Tools
233 tools (117 read-only / 116 write) across 14 domains. All write tools require native user approva
l. Every tool except `pve_sources` takes an optional `source` argument.
| Domain | Tools | Scope |

| Sources | 1 | list the configured Proxmox VE sources (never returns credentials) |
| Cluster & ove

rview | 8 | version, status, resources index, tasks, log, nextid, options |
| Nodes & tasks | 23 | s

tatus, config, services, disks, syslog, apt, SMART, task polling |
| Network | 12 | interface CRUD +

reload, DNS, hosts, time |
| VMs (QEMU) | 22 | config, power, snapshot, clone, migrate, resize, mov

e-disk, guest-agent, monitor |
| Containers (LXC) | 15 | config, power, snapshot, clone, migrate, re

size |
| Storage | 11 | CRUD, content/volumes, upload, RRD |
| Firewall | 76 | rules / aliases / ips

et / options / log across cluster·node·VM·CT scopes |
| Access control | 21 | users, groups, roles,

domains, ACL |
| Pools | 5 | resource pools |
| HA | 13 | resources, groups, status, migrate / reloc

ate |
| Backup | 6 | vzdump jobs + run-now |
| Replication | 9 | job CRUD, schedule-now, status / lo

g |
| Ceph | 11 | status, OSD, pools, MON / MDS / FS, logs |
See **docs/tools.md** for the full per-tool reference (name, method, path, description).
Async operations return a `UPID:...` task id — the agent polls `pve_task_status` / `pve_task_log` to
confirm completion.
## Security

- Mandatory approval on every write operation — the model cannot bypass it.
- Secrets, tokens, and p

asswords are redacted before any response reaches the model.
- All PVE-returned data is treated as u
ntrusted, never as instructions.
